solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Frantically fan the heir of a German physicist

indicators.note: acting frantically is wild and disordered, so these letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone madly fans the heir of a German scientist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Frantically' rearranges FAN THE HEIR, ten letters, into the scientist's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Daniel Gabriel Fahrenheit was a German-born physicist who devised the temperature scale bearing his name.

definitions.meaning: honest means just and above board
blonde hair is pale or light in colour

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both just and above board and, of hair, light-coloured.

parts.note: an animal's pelt is its coat of fur or hair
to spray something is to wet it with droplets

explanation.surface: Someone is pelted with a soaking of lacquer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pelt' looks like a verb (to throw things at), but it is the noun, an animal's coat.
explanation.definitionFit: Hair lacquer is the old name for the product sprayed on to hold a hairstyle in place.

clue.text: National emblem well under par of course

definitions.meaning: the bald bird of prey is the emblem of the USA, among other nations
on a golf course, a score two strokes under par on a hole

explanation.definitionFit: The bird appears as a national symbol, and golfers use the same name for a hole played two under par.

clue.text: She is an eccentric in cloth

indicators.note: an eccentric is odd or off-centre, so these letters are set out of their usual order

explanation.surface: A woman described as an eccentric in her choice of fabric.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eccentric' rearranges SHE IS AN into the fabric; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Hessian is a coarse woven fabric made from jute or hemp, used for sacking.

clue.text: Rascal and two other boys ran through

parts.note: an imp is a mischievous child, a little rascal
AL and ED are short boys' names, Albert or Alan and Edward
AL and ED are short boys' names, Albert or Alan and Edward

explanation.surface: A naughty child and a couple of his friends ran through somewhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ran through' suggests running past, but it means pierced as with a sword.
explanation.definitionFit: To be run through with a spear or sword is to be skewered, which is what this verb describes.

parts.note: a plant name that is also the coloured ring around the pupil, so a flower found in every eye

explanation.definitionFit: The same name is shared by a garden flower and the coloured part of the eye around the pupil.

indicators.note: to partake of something is to take a share of it, so the answer is a share taken from these words

explanation.surface: A bailiff took part in a gloomy night out.
explanation.definitionFit: A reeve was a medieval English official, a manor's steward or bailiff.

clue.text: Severe ward sister's first to the rear

parts.note: stern means strict or severe
taken as written

indicators.note: the first of sister's is the opening letter of that word

explanation.surface: A severe ward sister goes first to the back of the line.
explanation.definitionFit: Sternwards means towards the stern of a ship, the back end, so towards the rear.

clue.text: Chemical firm's no good in the cake-topping business

parts.note: ICI, Imperial Chemical Industries, was a major British chemical company; the 's means is

explanation.surface: A chemical company has no luck in the world of cake decoration.
explanation.walkthrough: ICI (Imperial Chemical Industries) was once Britain's best-known chemical company.
explanation.definitionFit: Icing is the sugary coating spread on top of cakes, so its making is the cake-topping business.

parts.note: SUPER is short for superintendent, a senior police officer

indicators.note: the word sound says the next piece is to be heard, not read

parts.note: seed in the biblical sense means offspring or descendants

explanation.surface: Someone throws out a police officer who comes with healthy offspring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sound' looks like an adjective (healthy) but signals a homophone: SEDE is said like SEED.
explanation.definitionFit: To supersede something is to replace it and set it aside, to discard it for something newer.

indicators.note: staggering here means reeling about, so the letters of the next word lurch into a new order

explanation.surface: A remarkable miracle is called back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'staggering' looks like 'amazing', describing the miracle, but it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To recall goods or land is to demand them back, which is to take them back as one's own.

definitions.meaning: a volunteer police officer in Britain, a part-time constable

explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis carries on from 10-across, where a policeman also appears. In Britain a special constable is a volunteer, unpaid police officer.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means out of the ordinary, and in Britain it is also short for a volunteer police constable.

clue.text: Nuclear reaction after ruthenium is extracted, unpolluted

indicators.note: a nuclear reaction rearranges what goes into it, so the letters of this word are reshuffled once something is taken away

parts.note: Ru is the chemical symbol for ruthenium

explanation.surface: A nuclear process leaves things unpolluted once ruthenium has been taken out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reaction' looks like part of the physics picture, but it signals rearranging; 'after ... is extracted' says the ruthenium symbol comes out of the fodder first.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unpolluted is free of dirt and contamination, which is to say spotless.

parts.note: the abbreviation for the state of Louisiana is also the familiar short name of a large Californian city, so that place is a 'Louisiana' in California

explanation.definitionFit: The city in southern California is commonly abbreviated LA, the same letters as the postal code for Louisiana.

clue.text: Perhaps one of the eight soars Manchester for a while

indicators.note: for a while says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone among eight people flies high over Manchester for a time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the eight' is a rowing crew of eight, as in the Oxford and Cambridge Boat Race.
explanation.definitionFit: A racing eight is a rowing boat with eight rowers, so any one of them is an example of a rower.

indicators.note: a question asked is spoken, so the words in quotes are to be heard rather than read

parts.note: said quickly, these two words give the French name

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether the month of May was dull and overcast.
explanation.walkthrough: Inspector Maigret is Georges Simenon's French police detective.
explanation.definitionFit: Jules Maigret is the fictional Paris police commissaire in Simenon's crime novels.

clue.text: Doctor starting at Cambridge University locates a bloodsucker

indicators.note: starting means taking the opening letter of each of the following words

explanation.surface: A doctor beginning work at Cambridge finds a parasite.
explanation.definitionFit: Bram Stoker's Count Dracula is a vampire, who feeds on blood, so a bloodsucker.

clue.text: A French Assembly Member stopped and left it as it was

parts.note: un is French for a
AM is the title of a member of the Welsh Assembly
ended means stopped or finished

explanation.surface: A French politician called a halt and changed nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: AM stands for Assembly Member, as the Welsh Assembly's members were known.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unamended has not been altered, so it has been left in its original form.

indicators.note: to create is to make something new out of material, so the letters are made into a new word

explanation.surface: A local facility gives rise to a moment that can come at any time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'creates' rearranges AMENITY.
explanation.definitionFit: The adverb means at whatever time, the same sense as whenever.

clue.text: Territory for 150 in Eastern part of church

indicators.note: in says one piece goes inside another

parts.note: the nave is the main body of a church
CL is 150 in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Ground set aside for 150 people in the east end of a church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' is a link here; '150' looks like a count of people, but it is a Roman numeral.
explanation.definitionFit: An enclave is a small territory entirely surrounded by another state's land.

clue.text: Order military leader with gallantry award a new date

parts.note: CO is short for ... officer
MM is the Military Medal, a British award for bravery

explanation.surface: Someone tells a decorated officer to set a different date.
explanation.walkthrough: MM is the Military Medal, a British award for gallantry.
explanation.definitionFit: To command is to give an instruction, the same as to order someone.

definitions.meaning: regains consciousness, wakes up after fainting
amounts to, as a bill reaching a total

explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means both regains consciousness and amounts to, as a sum totalling some figure.

clue.text: Soldier very nearly became a donor

parts.note: GI is an American soldier

indicators.note: nearly means not quite all of the word, so its last letter is cut

explanation.surface: A soldier almost turned into a generous benefactor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nearly' cuts the final Y off VERY; 'became' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A donor is one who gives something, such as blood or money, so a giver.

clue.text: Found item of food by way of starting new dish

parts.note: via means by way of

indicators.note: starting takes the opening letter of each of the next words

explanation.surface: Someone came across a dish of food via a new recipe.
explanation.definitionFit: A viand is an old word for an article of food, usually in the plural.

indicators.note: audibly says the next words give a word as it is heard

parts.note: a compere is a host or presenter, the anchor of a show

explanation.surface: Someone sounds like the presenter of a broadcast.
explanation.walkthrough: A compere (in Britain) is the host who introduces acts in a show.
explanation.definitionFit: To compare with is to be comparable to, to bear resemblance to, so the verb stands for resemble.

indicators.note: shortening a word trims its end, here the final letter of verse

explanation.surface: A poet announces that a verse has been cut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is shortened' drops the last E of VERSE.
explanation.definitionFit: To aver is to state firmly, so avers means declares.

indicators.note: U is the label for upper-class, socially acceptable usage, so non-U means the letter U is taken away

parts.note: an odour is a smell

explanation.surface: An American scent is said to have an offensive smell.
explanation.walkthrough: In crosswords U means upper-class or acceptable, so 'socially unacceptable' removes U. The 's means is; the result is the American spelling.
explanation.definitionFit: The US spelling drops the U, and a perfume is a scent or fragrance.

clue.text: However, began leaving Orient by road south

indicators.note: began here means the start of the following word

parts.note: the Orient is the East
a way is a road

explanation.surface: Someone set off from the East by road heading south.
explanation.definitionFit: The dialect adverb means at least or in any case, so serves as however.

definitions.meaning: put out, brought to an end

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses mean brought to a finish: a life extinguished and a lease that ran out are both over.

definitions.meaning: secondary or minor, as in a lesser issue
a point of view or aspect of a matter

explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective the word means secondary or minor, and as a noun an aspect or point of view.

indicators.note: something re-established is set up afresh, so these letters are set up in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone thinks again now that order has been restored.
explanation.walkthrough: 're-established' rearranges SINCE ORDER.
explanation.definitionFit: To reconsider is to think a matter over afresh, perhaps changing a decision.
